title: Half-Year Production Report 2026
gist: Glencore's H1 2026 own-sourced copper output rose 15% on stronger African Copper and Antamina grades, while cobalt fell 46% as DRC export quotas force prioritization of copper over cobalt, and zinc dropped 21% on the Lady Loretta closure and Kidd mine disposal; FY2026 copper and zinc guidance was held despite Kidd's removal, implying an effective like-for-like upgrade, and Marketing is set to post a strong ~$3.3bn H1 Adjusted EBIT.

themes.theme: Copper volume beat and a hidden guidance upgrade

insights.claim: Glencore's own-sourced copper production rose 15% year-on-year to 397,000 tonnes in H1 2026, driven by +55,000 tonnes from higher mining rates and grades at African Copper and +27,700 tonnes from higher grades at Antamina, partly offset by -20,400 tonnes from the planned July 2025 closure of Mount Isa.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Copper is Glencore's clear H1 volume winner and the main offset to weakness in zinc, cobalt and steelmaking coal; watch whether African Copper and Antamina grade tailwinds persist into H2.
insights.quote: the planned closure of the Mount Isa copper mine in July 2025 (20,400 tonnes)

insights.claim: Glencore held FY2026 copper guidance at 810-870kt even though the Kidd mine disposal (completed 1 June 2026) removes an assumed ~11kt of H2 copper production, which the company says implies an effective like-for-like upgrade to the underlying guidance mid-point.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The unchanged headline guidance understates underlying momentum; investors modeling copper volumes should add back the Kidd shortfall to get the true like-for-like trajectory.
insights.quote: implies a like-for-like upgrade in the guidance mid-points for these two commodities.

insights.claim: FY2026 copper production is weighted 53% to H2, with Collahuasi expected to contribute a higher H2 share on improved recoveries from primary ore and better mining performance.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: H2 copper delivery is unusually dependent on Collahuasi executing an operational improvement; a miss there would pressure full-year guidance more than in prior years.
insights.quote: higher expected recoveries from primary ore and an improved mining performance.

themes.theme: DRC cobalt export quotas force a copper-first tradeoff

insights.claim: Own-sourced cobalt production fell 46% year-on-year to 10,200 tonnes in H1 2026, as the DRC government's ongoing export quota regime forced Glencore to prioritize copper production over cobalt processing at its African operations.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Regulatory quotas, not geology or demand, are the binding constraint on Glencore's cobalt output; any DRC policy shift is a direct swing factor for global cobalt supply.
insights.quote: the DRC government's ongoing cobalt export quota regime, with operating activities requiring careful consideration of quota allocations, whereby prioritisation and focus is given to copper production.

insights.claim: Cobalt contained in mixed ore is increasingly being held in solution rather than processed and dried into saleable hydroxide, meaning Glencore is building a deferred cobalt inventory that will be processed and sold once DRC export regulations evolve.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: There is latent cobalt supply sitting off-market; a future loosening of DRC quotas could unlock a supply bump that caps cobalt prices faster than headline production trends suggest.
insights.quote: cobalt contained in mixed ore is increasingly being held in solution, rather than processed and dried into saleable cobalt in hydroxides.

themes.theme: Zinc: mine-life exits cut volume but unit costs turned negative

insights.claim: Zinc production fell 21% year-on-year to 365,600 tonnes, driven by Lady Loretta's end of mine life in late 2025 (-51,000 tonnes), lower zinc grades at Antamina as it phases toward higher copper/lower zinc grades (-39,200 tonnes), and the 1 June 2026 disposal of the Kidd mine.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Zinc's decline is structural (mine closures, grade phasing), not cyclical, so investors should not expect a rebound from current operations without new zinc capacity.

insights.claim: Zinc net unit cash cost turned negative at -8.5 c/lb in H1 2026, from +2.3 c/lb in H1 2025, meaning by-product credits now exceed direct cash costs for the zinc business.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Falling volumes are being offset by a sharply improved cost structure, so zinc segment profitability may hold up better than volume trends alone would suggest.

insights.claim: FY2026 zinc guidance was held at 700-740kt despite the Kidd mine disposal removing an assumed ~20kt of production and despite a May 2026 incident at Kazzinc's Ust-Kamenogorsk zinc dust collection unit, which the company says did not materially impact the guidance.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: As with copper, unchanged zinc guidance masks an effective like-for-like upgrade; the Kazzinc incident is flagged as immaterial, worth confirming in H2 disclosures for any lagged impact.
insights.quote: Overall zinc production guidance was not materially impacted by the May 2026 incident at Kazzinc’s Ust-Kamenogorsk zinc dust collection unit.

themes.theme: Coal split: steelmaking coal execution issues vs. energy coal curtailment and outperformance

insights.claim: Steelmaking coal production fell 14% year-on-year to 13.5 million tonnes due to lower EVR throughput and yields, which Glencore expects to normalise in H2 2026, partly offset by higher Australian volumes.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A production shortfall attributed to fixable operational issues (throughput/yield) rather than geology or market curtailment is a near-term watch item for H2 execution risk.
insights.quote: due to lower EVR production, primarily reflecting lower throughput and yields, which are expected to normalise in H2 2026

insights.claim: Energy coal production fell 2% year-on-year to 47.4 million tonnes due to the voluntary production curtailment at Cerrejón implemented from Q2 2025 in response to market conditions, yet H1 actual output beat prior guidance by roughly 3 million tonnes on stronger Australian portfolio performance, prompting Glencore to raise FY2026 guidance to 96-101mt.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Glencore is actively managing energy coal supply to market conditions via Cerrejón curtailment while Australian assets outperform, indicating discretionary supply flexibility investors can use to gauge the company's price sensitivity.
insights.quote: primarily reflecting the impact of the voluntary production curtailment implemented at Cerrejón from Q2 2025 in response to market conditions.

insights.claim: Steelmaking coal's FOB unit cash cost rose to $127.0/t in H1 2026 from $108.4/t in H1 2025 (+17%), and energy coal's FOB cost rose to $76.1/t from over $65.0/t, but both were outpaced by realized price gains (steelmaking coal realized price up to $206.9/t from $167.1/t, energy coal up to $93.9/t from $78.6/t), implying margin expansion in both coal lines despite cost inflation.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Coal segment margins are widening even as unit costs rise, because benchmark prices (PHCC, NEWC) rose faster than costs; this favors coal segment earnings even amid the H1 volume declines.
insights.locator: Estimated H1 unit costs / H1 realised prices

themes.theme: Copper unit costs fall despite Middle East-driven input inflation, Africa the standout

insights.claim: Glencore's copper net unit cash cost fell 13% to 208.4 c/lb in H1 2026 from 240.6 c/lb in H1 2025, reflecting an additional 78.6kt of copper production, partially offset by higher diesel, sulphuric acid, sulphur and freight costs tied to the Middle East conflict.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Volume growth is more than offsetting geopolitical input-cost inflation for copper, a positive operating-leverage signal; a further Middle East escalation would be the key risk to watch on the cost side.
insights.quote: positively reflects the copper department’s additional 78.6kt of copper production, partially offset by higher overall input costs due to the Middle East conflict, mainly relating to diesel, sulphuric acid, sulphur and freight.

insights.claim: African copper operations' net unit cash cost dropped sharply to 221.8 c/lb in H1 2026 from 353.4 c/lb in H1 2025, even though Africa absorbed the bulk of Middle East-related input cost inflation and did not benefit from record-low TC/RCs, because it prioritized copper output over cobalt.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The African copper business is delivering the largest single cost improvement in the portfolio, partly as a direct consequence of the DRC-driven pivot away from cobalt — a cross-commodity tradeoff investors should track together.
insights.quote: did not benefit from record low TC/RCs and managed its production around prioritisation of copper at the expense of lower cobalt production.

insights.claim: South America copper unit cash cost improved only modestly to 160.8 c/lb from 168.2 c/lb, leaving Africa (221.8 c/lb) still the higher-cost region despite its larger year-on-year improvement.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Regional cost convergence has not happened yet; South America remains the lower-cost copper base for Glencore, useful for modeling regional margin mix.

themes.theme: Realized prices trail benchmark indices across metals and coal

insights.claim: Glencore's H1 2026 realized copper price of $12,704/t was 3% below the average LME price of $13,084/t, and zinc's realized price of $3,284/t was 2% below the average LME price of $3,349/t, while nickel's realized price of $17,718/t was essentially in line with the LME average of $17,708/t.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Glencore consistently realizes slightly below LME benchmarks on copper and zinc, a modest but persistent discount to bake into revenue models rather than assuming full benchmark capture.

insights.claim: The portfolio mix discount versus benchmark indices widened year-on-year for both coal types: steelmaking coal's discount to the PHCC settlement price grew to -$29.9/t from -$17.6/t, and energy coal's discount to the NEWC settlement price grew to -$34.0/t from -$23.9/t.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: A widening quality/mix discount versus PHCC and NEWC benchmarks suggests Glencore's coal portfolio is skewing toward lower-quality grades, which caps realized upside even as headline coal indices rise.

themes.theme: Marketing segment strength cushions mixed industrial output

insights.claim: Glencore expects to report a strong H1 2026 Marketing Adjusted EBIT of approximately $3.3 billion, providing an earnings buffer against the mixed industrial production performance where zinc, cobalt and steelmaking coal volumes declined while copper rose.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Marketing earnings strength can offset industrial-segment volume softness, so investors should weight full-group earnings resilience above headline production misses in individual commodities.
insights.quote: we expect to report a strong half-year Marketing Adjusted EBIT of c.$3.3 billion.

themes.theme: Gold, silver, nickel and chrome: a steep unexplained gold shortfall

insights.claim: Gold production fell 44% year-on-year to 168koz from 301koz in H1 2026 — the steepest percentage decline of any commodity in the report — yet Glencore's H1 production highlights section offers no explanatory driver for the drop.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The largest percentage swing in the entire report is left unexplained in the narrative; investors should seek clarification (e.g., via the full PDF report or IR) before drawing conclusions about the gold by-product stream.

insights.claim: Silver production rose 2% year-on-year to 9,306koz from 9,097koz in H1 2026, a modest gain compared to the sharper moves in other by-product metals.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Silver is a minor but stable by-product stream for Glencore, unlikely to be a swing factor for the group's overall results.

insights.claim: Nickel production of 35,800 tonnes was broadly flat year-on-year (-2% versus 36.6kt in H1 2025), and FY2026 guidance remains unchanged at 70-80kt with a 52% H2 weighting.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: Nickel is the most stable of Glencore's base metals this period, offering limited surprise risk to full-year guidance.
insights.locator: H1 production highlights, nickel / 2026 production guidance

insights.claim: Attributable chrome ore production fell 4% year-on-year to 1,647,000 tonnes, a decline Glencore attributes only generically to 'operating conditions over the period' without further detail.
insights.speaker: Glencore investor reports
insights.so_what: The vague explanation for the chrome ore decline (versus the detailed mine-level attribution given for copper, zinc and coal) suggests it is a lower-priority disclosure item, but still worth flagging for South African ferrochrome supply-chain watchers.
insights.quote: reflecting the operating conditions over the period.
